newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Delhaize eyes Asia for market share.
newsitem.headline: Delhaize eyes Asia for market share.

text.p: Belgian retail group Delhaize, which owns retail chains in Europe and the United States sees Asia as an essential part of a future expansion drive.

"A growing company which wants to remain among the most important (retailers) must be present on these three (European, the U.S. and Asian) markets," said Delhaize chief executive Gui de Vaucleroy in an interview with newspaper L'Echo.
"Asia is going through an important development with consumer purchasing power improving. This is clearly one of our present concerns," Vaucleroy said.

Delhaize is studying the possibility of entering the Asian market. "We are also studying the possibility of finding a local partner. The Asian market was risky and if Delhaize decided to enter it would do so prudently. Vaucleroy said the results were due in 12 months.

Expansion into Asia would not be at the expense of U.S. and European market positions. Instead, positions in those markets would be strengthened. In the U.S. Delhaize's Food Lion recently bought Florida-based Kash n' Karry Food Stores in a $341 million deal.
